question: At what minimum distance should an object be held from the eyes for clear and comfortable viewing?
solution:
The correct answer is __**25 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The minimum distance at which an object can be seen most distinctly without any strain on the eyes is known as the **least distance of distinct vision (LDDV)**.
 
• For a **normal human eye** of a young adult, this distance is standardly measured to be **25 cm**.
 
• This specific distance is also referred to as the **near point** of the eye, which represents the closest limit of clear focus.
 
• To see objects at this distance, the **ciliary muscles** of the eye contract to increase the curvature of the **crystalline lens**, making it thicker and decreasing its **focal length**.
